analysis.title: The great silver washout
key_insights: Silver's weekly RSI fell from above 90 to 30 in almost a straight line. It has been lower only once since Covid.
Price has retraced to its original long-term trendline after a parabolic move. The 200-week moving average sits slightly below current levels.
Silver and the main solar ETF, TAN, trade closely together. Solar has been hit even harder than silver recently.
Silver and the DXY maintain an almost perfect inverse relationship. The note advises checking the dollar's direction before buying the dip in silver.
Net non-commercial positioning in silver has come down but remains at levels last seen when silver traded substantially higher.
Earlier this year silver traded spot up, vol up. It has flipped to spot down, vol up, which is atypical for silver, and investors are scrambling for downside protection.
risk_factors: Positioning remains relatively elevated after the sell-off, so further liquidation is possible.
A rising dollar would pressure silver given the near-perfect inverse relationship with the DXY.
Downside protection demand is lifting volatility.
charts_described: Silver weekly RSI has collapsed from above 90 to 30 in almost a straight line and has been lower only once since Covid.
Silver has retraced to its original long-term trendline, with the 200-week moving average slightly below current levels.
Silver and TAN trade in close tandem, with solar hit harder than silver lately.
Silver and the DXY show an almost perfect inverse relationship.
Silver net non-commercial positioning has come down recently but remains at levels last seen when silver traded substantially higher.
Silver volatility has moved from spot up, vol up earlier this year to spot down, vol up.
vol_and_positioning: Silver volatility rose during the sell-off, reversing the earlier spot up, vol up pattern to spot down, vol up.
Many investors were caught by surprise and are buying downside protection.
Net non-commercial positioning has fallen but is still at levels last seen when silver was trading substantially higher.
